title: SIMD batching strategy: generic framework vs per-prime kernels
description:
Microbenchmark per-prime hand-rolled bipedal SIMD kernels against a generic `BatchedBipedalLike

` framework on the dev host (AVX2 path), and produce a decision document selecting the winning strategy. ## Background The bipedal SIMD kernel can be either (a) per-prime hand-rolled (one `bipedal3_kernel.rs`, one `bipedal5_kernel.rs`, one `bipedal7_kernel.rs` with specialised AVX2/AVX-512 functions) or (b) a generic `BatchedBipedalLike` framework instantiated three times. (a) gives maximum perf-per-prime but more code; (b) gives less code but may sacrifice constant factor. This issue measures both via a microbench in `dev/research/simd_batching_bench/` and produces a decision document. The winning strategy is the input contract for the $\mathbb{F}_3$ kernel work and the $\mathbb{F}_5$/$\mathbb{F}_7$ kernel work. ## Success Criteria - [ ] [hard] `dev/research/simd_batching_bench/` exists and contains both per-prime and generic-framework prototypes for $\mathbb{F}_3$ (the $\mathbb{F}_3$ case is enough to make the decision). - [ ] [hard] The microbench measures cycles/op for `add`, `sub`, `mul` on lane batches of 64, 256, and 1024 $\mathbb{F}_3$ elements via both strategies on the dev host (AVX2 path). - [ ] [hard] `dev/plans/r4_simd_batching_decision.md` exists and is attached via `jit doc add`, naming the winning strategy with measured numbers. - [ ] [hard] If the gap is $< 1.2\times$ either way, the doc recommends the generic framework as the tie-break (less code).
